thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — embeddings-proxy p99 latency spike and elevated 5xx in prod-us-west1. Paged: @maria_cheng @devon_patel. Root: sudden burst of requests from partner-connector-3.

maria cheng: acked. jumping on bridge. see error vol spike on ingress LB.

devon patel: joining bridge. preliminary glance: HPA oscillation + rate-limiter thrash. Autoscaler was scaling up then down repeatedly.

jules park: oncall bridge link?

maria cheng: bridge: https://zoom/bridge/xyz (not public) — i've started a short-term mitigation plan: 1) enable emergency client-level throttles, 2) warm the dedicated pool (if possible), 3) fallback to smaller model variant for non-critical routes.

neil ortiz: logs show repeated 429 then retries exploding into 5xx from proxy. sample logs: 
```
2026-02-15T14:22:01Z embeddings-proxy ERROR request_id=abc123 status=429 client=partner-connector-3 retry=0
2026-02-15T14:22:01Z embeddings-proxy ERROR request_id=abc124 status=503 backend=embed-worker-7 reason=kv-cache-miss
```

samir khan: quick check: kubectl get hpa embeddings-proxy -o yaml shows minReplicas:2 maxReplicas:40 cpu target 60% with very short scale down window. we probably need longer stabilization.

maria cheng: applying temp rate-limit config now (`/etc/redwood/ratelimits/global.yaml`) to cap partner-connector-3 to 10rps.

sre-bot: actioned: rate-limit updated for partner-connector-3 -> 10rps. autoscaler cooldown increased to 300s (temp). Warm pool request sent to dedicated-team.

devon patel: routing ~20% of traffic to canary-model (smaller) for non-critical evals. This drops median latency from 450ms -> 220ms for those flows.

anne (cs): any customer-visible failures? which tenants affected?

maria cheng: initial estimate: ~12 enterprise tenants experienced elevated latency for embeddings and a handful got 5xx for up to ~18 minutes before throttles. larger customers behind partner-connector-3 saw most of the failures. CS will reach out.

anne (cs): on it. prepping a short note: timeline, impact, mitigation steps. will wait for postmortem for root cause details.

jules park: good. recording owner for postmortem: @jules_park. will lead RCA and timeline. proposed postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 PT.

neil ortiz: immediate post-incident action items I see: 
- pin autoscaler stabilization to 5m
- add client-specific burst detection alert (not just p99)
- dedupe pager rules so repeated 5xx/429 from same client don't generate new pages every minute
- add a synthetic canary for partner-connector-3 traffic pattern

devon patel: agree. also need a safer fallback routing: if kv-cache miss rate > 8% and p99 > 2s, auto-route to smaller model variant and send an alert but don't page.

maria cheng: adding temporary TODOs in incident tracker.

sre-bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-042 with summary and linked mitigation steps. assigned to jules park.

jules park: posting proposed timeline for postmortem doc and invites:
- doc ready by EOD today with logs, spans, and timeline
- meeting tomorrow 09:30 PT (60m)
- pre-reads: autoscaler metrics, ingress logs, quota/rate-limit changes

lee (product): please include any product-config flags changed and which customers might have feature gating that triggers different code paths. we need to know if product-side deploys made this worse.

samir khan: quick config snippet i ran to inspect rate limiter state:
```
# show top clients by request rate
redis-cli zrevrange ratelimit:clients 0 10 withscores
```

samir khan: partner-connector-3 showed a 10x spike at 14:21 UTC. no deploys from product within last 3 hours. looks like partner test traffic.

maria cheng: mitigation timeline:
- 14:22 enabled client throttle 10rps (reduced failures)
- 14:25 increased autoscaler cooldown to 300s (reduced oscillation)
- 14:28 warmed 10 nodes in dedicated pool
- 14:33 switched 20% traffic to smaller-model canary
- 14:40 error rate dropped to baseline, p99 reduced by 60%

anne (cs): sending notify to affected customers: short summary + ETA for postmortem. will update once jules posts document.

jules park: assigning owners for action items:
- Autoscaler stabilization and HPA config: @samir_khan (due in 2 weeks)
- Pager dedupe + alert rewrite: @devon_patel (due in 1 week)
- Client burst detection synthetic: @neil_ortiz (due in 2 weeks)
- Runbook: emergency throttles + fallback routing: @maria_cheng (due in 1 week)
- CS customer follow-ups doc: @anne (cs) (initial outreach done, full follow-up after RCA)

lee (product): +1 on runbook. product to review if any feature flags could cause partner to send unusual payloads. assigned to me, sync with jules after doc posted.

devon patel: follow-up on alerts: propose new combined alert condition: if p99 > 2s AND 5xx_rate > 1% across >5% of tenants AND unique top client spikes > 3x baseline => page on-call; otherwise create high-severity ticket with slack-only notification. this should cut noise from partner bursts that are mitigated by throttles.

maria cheng: will add that to postmortem recommendations.

jules park: doc link (draft): https://docs.internal.redwood/postmortems/INC-2026-042 (please add logs, spans, and any relevant dashboards).

sre-bot: reminder: schedule follow-up check-in in 2 weeks to verify action items. created calendar event: Post-incident follow-up (INC-2026-042) 2026-03-01 10:00 PT.

neil ortiz: a couple of small monitoring changes I'll push today:
- add rate-of-change alert for top-client request counters
- increase retention for gateway request traces for 48h (was 6h)

samir khan: will open PR to lock HPA scale-down-window and document recommended values in infra repo.

anne (cs): closing loop: I notified 12 tenants at 15:05 PT with summary and link to postmortem draft. will update customers after RCA.

maria cheng: thanks all. nice fast mitigation. postmortem owner @jules_park — please include clear SLO impact calc and proposed new paging rule thresholds.

jules park: noted. will post final doc by EOD and send meeting invite.

maria cheng: resolved: system at baseline at 14:40; monitoring stable. closing incident in pager system. :white_check_mark:
